text.p: The UK's FTSE 100 index was trading around its 4,400 resistance level on Thursday and a breach of that level could be the springboard for an assault on its all-time high, chart analysts said.
The blue chip index was up 12.1 points at 4,399.8 by 0849 GMT but had failed in the last two sessions to break through 4,400.
Independent chartist Brian Marber said the FTSE 100 chart looked technically positive. "The short-term indicators are good and the FTSE is being supported by the U.S. market," said Marber.
"Of course you are likely to see potential resistance at the 4,444 level, it happens everytime an index nears its all-time high but there is nothing wrong with this chart."
George MacLean at MMS International said the FTSE needed to consolidate after its recent sharp gains before taking a run at its record highs of last month.
The index set an intraday record of 4,466.3 on March 11. Its record close of 4,444.3 was set the same day.
